what: Plays once when the title’s top edge touches the screen center — each letter drops in from 1rem above, squashed to .7 vertically and transparent, then springs upright with elastic.out(1, .6) over 1.35s. .05s between letters, with sine.inOut on the stagger too, so a wave seems to sweep across the title — over a dark photo, in the vertical closing line and copy lines

options.drop: Initial upward offset distance — with unit (-1rem · -24px · -2vw), a bare number is px, default -1rem
options.squash: Initial vertical scale (top edge axis), default .7 — at 1 it is not squashed
options.ease: Curve — GSAP name (with parentheses, elastic.out(1, 0.6)) or 0.22,1,0.36,1, default elastic.out(1, 0.6)
options.order-ease: Curve applied to the stagger (GSAP stagger ease), default sine.inOut — none means even

use: Your title first line hereSecond row
note: Inner line span and br stay as they are and only the text nodes are split. Split characters get aria-hidden, and the heading carries the original text as aria-label

from.where: index.html .lp-daily__ttl (three-line copy over a dark keyboard photo) — the SVG letter paths of the original .js-inveiw-important go from y -1rem·opacity 0·scaleY .7 → 0, 1.35s elastic.out(1, 0.6), stagger { each .05, from start, ease sine.inOut }, top center once
